title: When the Silence Sings
premise: Isandro Amberdale, once a piano prodigy whose hands failed him at nineteen, returns to the conservatory that made and unmade him — this time pushing a mop cart through its marble corridors. When the crumbling house where he grew up with his late mother goes up for auction, Isandro is forced to walk through its rooms one last time, cataloguing what memory has kept and what it has quietly stolen. As the auction date approaches, they must finally speak the goodbye they never managed, out loud, before the last traces of their mother's voice fade from recall. The novel ends not with Isandro buying the house, but with them playing — badly, freely — in its emptied front room, choosing the living over the preserved.
about_author: Ivo Galloway is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian who wrote this novel during night shifts, on the backs of work orders. They live in a coastal town where they teach an informal piano class for adults who were told, once, that they had no talent.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Establishes the daily rhythm of janitorial work at the conservatory: mopping the stage where they once debuted, avoiding the practice rooms, exchanging careful small talk with a teenage student named Wren who plays like Isandro used to. Emotional beat: quiet self-erasure, the ache of proximity to a former life.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A legal letter arrives: the childhood house, held in trust since the mother's death, will be auctioned in six weeks. Isandro has one weekend of access to collect belongings. Flashback fragments surface unbidden — the metronome, the smell of turpentine, the mother's humming. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Wren Asks About the Piano
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers a plaque with Isandro's name in the conservatory lobby and corners the janitor with blunt questions. Isandro deflects, but the encounter cracks something open. Wren, hiding their own family trouble, begins lingering after hours. Emotional beat: reluctant connection, the first crack in the silence.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The first visit to the house. Isandro inventories objects for the auctioneer and finds the mother's unfinished letters — to Isandro, never sent, dated after the breakdown. Memory begins to blur: was the humming real, or invented? Emotional beat: grief arriving late and sideways.

chapters.title: What the Auctioneer Knows
chapters.summary: Auctioneer Marguerite Osei's POV. A pragmatic, unsentimental woman who has seen a thousand families dismantle themselves, Marguerite recognizes Isandro's paralysis and gently refuses to let them hide behind paperwork. She shares a story of her own lost home. Emotional beat: unexpected mercy from a stranger; the stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: Practice Room 7
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren coaxes Isandro into a practice room after hours and asks them to demonstrate a passage. Isandro's hands shake; they play four bars and stop. Wren confesses they may lose their scholarship and their only safe place. Emotional beat: two silences recognizing each other; found family begins.

chapters.title: The Letters, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro returns to the house at night and reads the mother's letters aloud in the empty kitchen — the 'out loud' the blurb promises begins. A memory returns with terrible clarity: the night of the failed debut, and what the mother actually said. Emotional beat: devastation and release braided together; the midpoint turn.

chapters.title: Bidding War
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro and Marguerite POVs. Auction day. A developer drives the price beyond anything Isandro can reach; Wren shows up uninvited to stand beside them. Isandro bids until the money runs out, then stops — and the loss, strangely, feels clean. Emotional beat: climax; surrender transformed into choice.

chapters.title: The Empty Front Room
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The house stands vacant before handover. Isandro breaks in (with Marguerite's complicit key), drags the one unsold object — the mother's broken metronome — to the front room, and plays the piece from their debut on a borrowed keyboard, badly, laughing, crying. Emotional beat: the goodbye completed; the body forgiven.

chapters.title: Someone Has to Keep the Lights On
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, closing. Weeks later: Wren passes their recital; Isandro attends, sitting in the audience rather than the wings. Isandro offers to teach Wren for free, and accepts a small role accompanying the conservatory's community classes. The silence no longer sings of loss — it simply sings. Emotional beat: resolution; found family, chosen survival.
